description: Our idea with AstroDeepSpace is to create a software that uses AI to monitor astronauts' health during space missions. We want it to collect and analyze biometric data, detect unusual changes, and provide useful information, alerts, and recommendations about the astronaut's health. We also want to include cybersecurity to encrypt and protect their personal and medical data. We're looking for people interested in AI, programming, cybersecurity, and space exploration.
summary:
Our project, AstroDeepSpace, created HELIOS, a website designed to support astronauts' physical and mental health before, during, and after space missions.

Living in space can be challenging because astronauts may experience stress, sleep problems, and health changes. Getting medical help can also be difficult when they are far from Earth.
HELIOS helps organize health information, monitor vital signs, track daily well-being, and show medical alerts. It also includes Quirón, an AI assistant that helps users find information and understand the system.

We used simulated health data and scientific research from NASA to develop our prototype. We also tested its main features, privacy, and AI responses to identify areas for improvement.
Our goal is to make health monitoring easier, protect personal information, and help astronauts receive better support throughout their missions. We believe HELIOS could help make future space exploration safer and more organized for everyone.
details:
Through research, creativity, teamwork, and technology, we developed HELIOS, a platform designed to support astronaut health and well-being.

Our project combines software development, artificial intelligence, and space-related research to explore new ways of supporting astronauts during long-duration missions.

How does HELIOS work?

HELIOS brings important health information together in one place. Astronauts can complete daily health check-ins, review vital signs, and see alerts when something may need attention. The platform also includes different spaces for crew members, medical professionals, and other mission roles.

We developed Quiron, an AI assistant that helps users find information, understand the platform, and ask questions about their mission. The system is designed to respect privacy and keep medical decisions under human supervision.


What technologies did we use?

We used React to build the website, NestJS for the backend, and Supabase with PostgreSQL for database integration. We also integrated Google Gemini into Quiron.

The frontend is hosted on Vercel, while the backend runs on Render. We tested communication between both services and confirmed that the backend can connect to Supabase. Some database storage features still need further verification.


What makes our project different?

HELIOS focuses on three important stages:
Preparation before launch, health monitoring during the mission, and follow-up after returning to Earth.

We also considered communication problems, emotional well-being, medical privacy, and the importance of reliable information.

For our prototype, we created simulated astronaut profiles and health measurements. We also used scientific documentation from NASA to understand health risks such as sleep problems and fatigue.


Testing and future impact

We completed 13 tests to evaluate the website, health features, privacy controls, and AI responses. These tests helped us identify working features and areas that need improvement. We believe HELIOS could help astronauts recognize health problems earlier, organize medical information, and receive better support during long missions. Our goal is to contribute to safer space exploration by making astronaut health monitoring more accessible, organized, and focused on human well-being.

Note: To access the HELIOS project, click on "Enter Simulation" on the website. We also have a "Documents" section where you can find more detailed information about the project. Thank you for your interest in HELIOS!
